entries.name: Bevy
entries.use_for: Build games in Rust with a data-driven ECS engine.
entries.why: Leading Rust engine with a fast-moving ecosystem and modular plugin design.
entries.summary: Data-driven game engine in Rust using the Entity Component System paradigm. Provides 2D and 3D features in a modular plugin architecture, aimed to be simple for newcomers and flexible for power users.
entries.best_for: Rust developers building 2D/3D games or simulations who want code-first ECS architecture and a growing plugin ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Fast-moving APIs with frequent breaking changes and no full visual editor; not for teams wanting an editor-driven workflow.

entries.name: Ebitengine
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Go for desktop, mobile, web and consoles.
entries.why: The standard Go game engine; simple API, ships on Nintendo Switch.
entries.summary: Open source 2D game engine for Go with a simple API. Supports 2D graphics with matrix transforms, offscreen rendering, text, audio and input, and deploys to desktop, mobile, web and consoles.
entries.best_for: Go developers making 2D games that should ship across desktop, mobile, web and consoles with minimal dependencies.
entries.not_for: 2D only and code-only with no editor; not for 3D or teams wanting a built-in scene tool.

entries.name: Excalibur
entries.use_for: Build 2D web games in TypeScript with a full engine (scenes, physics, input).
entries.why: TypeScript-first 2D engine (~2.4k stars, BSD-2) with good docs and tooling.
entries.summary: Free TypeScript game engine for 2D games on HTML5 canvas. Offers scenes, actors, physics, input and tooling, aimed at both newcomers and experienced developers.
entries.best_for: TypeScript developers building 2D browser games who want a typed, structured engine with scenes and physics.
entries.not_for: 2D web only; smaller community than Phaser and no 3D support.

entries.name: Flame
entries.use_for: Build 2D games on Flutter for mobile, web and desktop.
entries.why: The main Flutter game engine with components, collisions and many bridge packages.
entries.summary: Flutter-based 2D game engine providing a game loop, component system, effects and particles, collision detection, gesture and input handling, and sprite/animation support. Extended by bridge packages for other libraries.
entries.best_for: Flutter developers building 2D games for mobile, web and desktop within the Flutter toolchain.
entries.not_for: Tied to Flutter/Dart and 2D; not for 3D or heavy graphics-intensive games.

entries.name: Fyrox
entries.use_for: Make 2D and 3D games in Rust with a scene editor.
entries.why: Feature-rich Rust engine that ships with a full editor, unlike most Rust engines.
entries.summary: General purpose 2D/3D game engine in Rust with a built-in scene editor. Includes browser-runnable examples and an official book.
entries.best_for: Rust developers who want an editor-based workflow for 2D and 3D games rather than assembling plugins.
entries.not_for: Smaller community and ecosystem than Bevy or Godot; Rust-only scripting.

entries.name: GDevelop
entries.use_for: Make 2D/3D games with an event-based, no-code editor that exports to web and mobile.
entries.why: Open-source no-code engine (~28k stars); Core, GDJS and IDE are MIT.

license_verified.note: Core, GDJS, IDE and Extensions folders are MIT; name and logo are trademarks

entries.summary: No-code, open-source game engine for 2D, 3D and multiplayer games using an event-based system and modular behaviors. Exports to mobile, desktop and web, with AI assistance features.
entries.best_for: Beginners, designers and prototypers who want to make games without writing code, or quickly ship web and mobile games.
entries.not_for: Not for code-first teams or very large or complex games; event-sheet logic can get unwieldy and some AI/cloud features are tied to a hosted service.

entries.name: Godot
entries.use_for: Make 2D and 3D games with a full editor, GDScript or C#.
entries.why: Most popular open-source game engine (119k stars); MIT, no royalties, exports to all major platforms.
entries.summary: Cross-platform 2D and 3D game engine with a unified editor, GDScript and C# scripting, and one-click export to desktop, mobile, web and consoles. MIT licensed with no royalties.
entries.best_for: General game development from solo indie to small teams, with a full editor and broad platform export.
entries.not_for: Not for AAA-scale 3D fidelity; console export requires third-party porting, and the engine has a large footprint versus lightweight code-only libraries.

entries.name: KAPLAY
entries.use_for: Make 2D browser games quickly with a fun, beginner-friendly JS library.
entries.why: Community successor to Kaboom.js (~1.8k stars, MIT) with an active release cadence.
entries.summary: Fun-first 2D game library for JavaScript and TypeScript, successor to Kaboom.js. Composes game objects from simple components and ships a web editor (KAPLAYGROUND) with 90+ examples.
entries.best_for: Beginners, game jams and quick browser game prototypes in JS/TS.
entries.not_for: 2D only with a simple component model; not suited to large complex games or 3D.

entries.name: libGDX
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform Java games for desktop, Android, iOS and web.
entries.why: Long-standing, mature JVM game framework with a large community.
entries.summary: Cross-platform Java game framework based on OpenGL (ES) targeting Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, web and iOS. Provides low-level building blocks without imposing a specific structure.
entries.best_for: Java/Kotlin developers building 2D or simple 3D games across desktop and mobile with a mature framework.
entries.not_for: Code-only framework with no editor and you assemble your own architecture; web and iOS backends are more involved than native tooling.

entries.name: LÖVE
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Lua with a small, fast framework.
entries.why: Beloved Lua 2D framework (~9k stars, zlib) behind many indie hits like Balatro.

license_verified.note: license.txt: LOVE is zlib; bundled deps have own licenses

entries.summary: Framework for making 2D games in Lua, running on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Documented via a wiki, with forums and an active community.
entries.best_for: Small 2D games, prototypes and jam projects written in Lua with a minimal API.
entries.not_for: 2D only, code-first with no editor; main branch is for the next major release and is not stable.

entries.name: MonoGame
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform 2D/3D games in C# with an XNA-style framework.
entries.why: Proven framework behind Stardew Valley and Celeste; Ms-PL licensed.
entries.summary: Open-source .NET framework for cross-platform 2D and 3D games in C#, a re-implementation of Microsoft XNA. Targets desktop, consoles and mobile, and has shipped titles like Celeste and Stardew Valley.
entries.best_for: C# developers wanting a code-first, XNA-style framework for 2D games across desktop, console and mobile.
entries.not_for: Framework, not an editor-driven engine; you build tooling and scene management yourself, and console targets require platform access.

entries.name: Open 3D Engine
entries.use_for: Build AAA-scale 3D games and simulations on an open engine.
entries.why: Linux Foundation engine from Amazon Lumberyard (~10k stars), Apache-2.0 or MIT.

license_verified.note: LICENSE.txt: Apache-2.0, or MIT at your option

entries.summary: Open-source, real-time, multi-platform 3D engine for AAA games, cinematic 3D worlds and high-fidelity simulations, without fees. Linux Foundation project derived from Amazon Lumberyard.
entries.best_for: Teams building high-fidelity 3D games or simulations that need a large open engine with no royalties and C++ extensibility.
entries.not_for: Heavy footprint and steep learning curve; overkill for small or 2D projects.

entries.name: Panda3D
entries.use_for: Build 3D games and simulations in Python with a C++ core.
entries.why: Mature 3D engine (~5k stars, BSD-3) originally from Disney and Carnegie Mellon.

license_verified.note: LICENSE: modified BSD (3-clause), Carnegie Mellon University

entries.summary: Game engine and framework for 3D rendering and game development using Python and C++. Free for any purpose, including commercial use, under a liberal license, with docs and samples.
entries.best_for: Python developers building 3D games, simulations or visualizations who want a mature engine with a C++ core.
entries.not_for: No full visual editor and fewer modern rendering features than major commercial engines; smaller community.

entries.name: Phaser
entries.use_for: Make 2D browser games with Canvas and WebGL.
entries.why: The most popular HTML5 2D game framework (40k stars) with extensive examples.
entries.summary: HTML5 game framework with WebGL and Canvas rendering for desktop and mobile browsers. Supports JavaScript or TypeScript, many front-end frameworks, and targets like Discord Activities and YouTube Playables.
entries.best_for: Browser-based 2D games in JS/TS with a large example library and community.
entries.not_for: 2D only; native mobile/desktop distribution relies on third-party wrappers; code-only without a built-in editor.

entries.name: pygame-ce
entries.use_for: Make 2D games in Python on top of SDL.
entries.why: Actively maintained community fork of pygame (370+ contributors), drop-in compatible.

license_verified.note: README states LGPL-2.1-or-later; text in docs/LGPL.txt

entries.summary: Community fork of pygame for 2D games in Python on top of SDL, with active maintenance and drop-in compatibility with pygame.
entries.best_for: Python developers building 2D games, prototypes or teaching projects, including migrating from pygame.
entries.not_for: Low-level and 2D-focused; not suited to 3D or very performance-heavy games, and has no editor.

entries.name: raylib
entries.use_for: Program games in C (or 70+ language bindings) with a simple, dependency-free API.
entries.why: Famously easy to learn; great for prototypes, jams and teaching. Zlib license.
entries.summary: Simple, dependency-free C library for game programming, inspired by Borland BGI and XNA, with bindings for 70+ languages. Suited to prototyping, tooling, education and embedded systems.
entries.best_for: Learning game programming, jams, prototypes and graphical tools in C or many other languages.
entries.not_for: No editor, visual tools or built-in scene system; you write everything in code.

entries.name: Ren'Py
entries.use_for: Build visual novels and story-driven games with a Python-based script language.
entries.why: The standard visual novel engine (~7k stars) behind thousands of commercial titles.

license_verified.note: Ren'Py itself MIT per sphinx/source/license.rst; some bundled parts LGPL

entries.summary: Visual novel engine with a Python-based scripting language. The standard tool for story-driven games, with a fix branch for stable releases and docs on renpy.org.
entries.best_for: Visual novels and dialogue-heavy story games, including commercial releases.
entries.not_for: Specialized for visual novels; not for action, physics-heavy or general 3D games.

entries.name: Stride
entries.use_for: Make 3D games in C# with a full editor.
entries.why: MIT-licensed C# engine with editor; an open alternative for Unity developers.
entries.summary: Open-source C# game engine for realistic rendering and VR, with a visual editor (Game Studio) for managing content. Modular design.
entries.best_for: C# developers wanting an editor-based 3D engine with strong rendering, as an open alternative to Unity.
entries.not_for: Smaller community and fewer learning resources than Unity or Godot; heavier for simple 2D games.
